name: Eurocentrism
summary: Eurocentrism is a worldview that treats Europe or the West as the centre of world events and as superior to other cultures. Its scholarly critics describe a linear theory of progress, a claim to universal truths drawn from European experience, and a justification of European colonial dominance. It is defined by its critics as a bias in knowledge, so it takes few positions on concrete policy questions.
scope: Eurocentrism as the worldview described in the defining scholarship (Amin, Wallerstein, Quijano, Dussel and reference entries): the assumption that European or Western history and values are normal and superior, with its linked universalism and theory of progress. It excludes the critics' own programmes (postcolonial, decolonial) and Western policies in general.
